name: Älvsåker - Stensjön

officialSources.title: West Sweden Trails: 1. Älvsåker - Stensjön
findings: Current official display name is Älvsåker - Stensjön.
Distance 26 km, estimated time 7-8 h, difficulty blue/medium.
Stage starts at Älvsåker in Kungsbacka where Bohusleden and Hallandsleden meet, then continues through Mölndal to Stensjön/Gunnebo.
Official page highlights Bunketorp, Kikås Långvatten, Herkulesgården, Gunnebo Slott, Sagsjön bird tower, and Livereds kulturstig.
Access notes name Anneberg station, Älvsåkersgården bus stop, start parking, and Gunnebo Park bus stop.

campingAndShelterNotes: No official separate campsite category was confirmed for Stage 1; the WST campsite widget did not yield importable campsite records in the facilities pass.
Overnight-capable shelters/rest areas on or near the route include Blåvättnerna, Stora Tjärnet, Horsickan, and possibly Hårssjön Rambo mosse shelter depending local reserve rules and signage.
Gunnebo kulturreservat forbids camping, wind shelters, and caravans; do not present Gunnebo as an overnight option.
A 2025 field diary reported no tent spot directly around Blåvättnerna shelter, even though the shelter was being used overnight by others.
fireNotes: Use only designated/prepared fireplaces where local rules allow and always check current fire bans before travel.

On 2026-04-29, the rules/safety lane found no current formal fire ban for Kungsbacka, Mölndal, or Härryda via the Länsstyrelserna/Krisinformation fire-ban map, but this is volatile and must be rechecked before publication.
Hårssjön-Rambo mosse allows fire only at prepared/signed fireplaces; portable grills/gas/alcohol stoves are excepted by the source summary.
Gunnebo rules differ in wording: Länsstyrelsen says fire only at designated places, while Gunnebo local page is stricter in practice; use the stricter local rule pending confirmation.

general: Allemansrätten applies, but local nature/cultural reserve rules override general access rights.
Dogs require extra strict supervision from 1 March to 20 August; several municipalities/reserves require leash. Mölndal says dogs are always leashed in nature reserves and municipal exercise tracks.
Fire-ban and forest-fire-risk status is volatile and must be rechecked live before publication or import-facing recommendations.

protectedAreas.name: Hårssjön-Rambo mosse naturreservat
protectedAreas.evidence: Länsstyrelsen states Bohusleden enters the reserve northwestern part and continues north; official GPX corridor around km 19-23 supports the crossing, but exact boundary intersection should be polygon-verified.
rules: Dogs must be leashed, except working dogs for livestock management or hunting.
Fires only at prepared/signed fireplaces; portable grills/gas/alcohol stoves excepted in the source summary.
Do not move or damage dead wood.
Avoid activities damaging vegetation or disturbing bird/wildlife on Rambo mosse and Hårskeröds mosse.
Events over 200 participants require Länsstyrelsen permit.

protectedAreas.name: Gunnebo kulturreservat
protectedAreas.evidence: Official stage text says the route crosses Gunnebo House grounds near the end. Gunnebo cultural reserve lies between Stensjön and Rådasjön and covers about 100 ha.
rules: No camping, wind shelters, or caravans.
Fires only at designated places per Länsstyrelsen; Gunnebo local page should be treated as stricter pending final verification.
Do not collect/damage plants, mosses, lichens or insects.
Do not capture or harm animals.
Do not enter sensitive marked areas.
protectedAreas.livestock: Gunnebo notes cows may be present in fields and working horses are used for estate management; keep dogs leashed and give livestock distance.

protectedAreas.name: Rådasjöns naturreservat
protectedAreas.statusForStage: possibly crossed or immediately adjacent near Gunnebo/Stensjön; verify before import
protectedAreas.evidence: Rådasjön reserve is tied to the Gunnebo/Råda landscape, and the reserve decision map labels Bohusleden near Gunnebo/Herkulesgården. Stage 1 GPX endpoint is at Stensjön, so exact Stage 1 overlap versus Stage 2 continuation is ambiguous.
rulesIfApplicable: Fires only at municipal prepared places.
Do not damage trees/dead wood or collect protected flora/fungi/lichens.

huntingForestryLivestock: No stage-specific hunting or forestry closures were found in the official and field-report passes.
Gunnebo may have cows and working horses; dogs should remain leashed and livestock given distance.

activeClosureStatus.finding: No active closures found in official trail/protected-area pages during this pass.
activeClosureStatus.caveat: Must be rechecked before runtime import or publication because closures and fire conditions change.

conditionReports.summary: Most recent visible activity on 2026-04-25 had no text details. 2025 reports are mostly good/great, with one fair report on 2025-02-22. Several hikers note the first part is asphalt/gravel or ordinary road, later changing to better forest/nature trail.
navigationNotes: 2025-08-24 review says the first 3 km differs from the official route while the remaining route follows the new path/markings.
2021-06-06 review mentions weak signage in places and accidental extra loop around Gunnebo.
difficultyNotes: Field reports call the stage demanding because of length and ups/downs despite official blue/moderate grading.
facilityNotes: 2024-05-01 report says two shelters were in very good condition and had firewood.

conditionReports.source: Wikiloc user track by Joakim Ernelind
conditionReports.summary: Recent user-recorded track reports 15.49 mi, moving time 5h19m, elapsed 6h18m, moderate technical difficulty. Useful as real-world pacing/track comparison, not primary geometry.

Start/end highlight notes Bohusleden starts and Hallandsleden ends in the Älvsåker/Blåvättnerna area, with a comfortable shelter and barbecue. Gunnebo highlight says park is suitable for relaxed walking/running and open all seasons; commercial services still need official opening-hour checks.
